title: Activation Functions
overview: Activation functions inject nonlinearity so networks can learn more than linear maps. The choice affects gradient flow, convergence speed and output range.
objectives: Compare sigmoid, tanh, ReLU and GELU
Explain vanishing gradients and dying ReLU
Choose an activation for hidden and output layers

method.title: Sigmoid and tanh
method.body: They squash values into bounded ranges but saturate, which shrinks gradients in deep stacks.

method.title: ReLU family
method.body: ReLU = max(0, x) has a constant gradient for positive inputs; Leaky ReLU keeps a small slope for negatives to avoid dead units.

method.title: GELU and SiLU
method.body: Smooth ReLU-like functions widely used in transformers and modern CNNs.

method.title: Output layers
method.body: Use sigmoid for binary probabilities, softmax for multi-class, and no activation for regression.

pseudocode:
sigmoid(x) = 1 / (1 + exp(-x))
tanh(x) = (exp(x) - exp(-x)) / (exp(x) + exp(-x))
relu(x) = max(0, x)
leaky_relu(x) = x if x > 0 else 0.01 * x
softmax(z)_i = exp(z_i - max(z)) / sum_j exp(z_j - max(z))

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
x = np.array([-2.0, -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 2.0])
sigmoid = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-x))
relu = np.maximum(0, x)
print("x      ", x)
print("sigmoid", np.round(sigmoid, 3))
print("tanh   ", np.round(np.tanh(x), 3))
print("relu   ", relu)
print("sigmoid grad max:", 0.25)
